headline: Goldman Flags Historic Discount in Mag 7 Upside Options
lede: Goldman Sachs's equity derivatives desk has recorded the largest discount ever in the implied volatility of upside call options for the Magnificent Seven basket relative to the Nasdaq-100 single-stock average. The spread, which has historically run at a premium reflecting the mega-cap group's outsized index weight and institutional hedging demand, is now its deepest below zero — meaning it is cheaper, in options-market terms, to bet on Mag 7 upside than on the upside of a typical Nasdaq name.
body:
Goldman Sachs (GS) tracks the spread between the average *implied volatility* on 25-delta call options — out-of-the-money contracts priced as bets on upside — for the **Magnificent Seven** basket and the equivalent average across Nasdaq-100 single stocks more broadly. The group — Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT), Alphabet (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), Meta Platforms (META), Nvidia (NVDA), and Tesla (TSLA) — has for most of the past decade commanded a premium: the market has charged more to bet on Mag 7 upside than on an average NDX constituent's upside, a differential justified by the basket's outsized index weight, binary earnings events, and relentless institutional hedging demand. That premium has now inverted.

As of mid-May 2026, the spread sits at -9.61 *vol points* — meaning Mag 7 upside calls are cheaper, not dearer, than the NDX average. The historical mean since 2014 is +4.15 and the prior record high was +14.11, putting the swing from peak to current trough at roughly 23 vol points — through zero to the deepest discount the firm has ever recorded. The signal is not a tenor-specific artifact: the inversion holds across one-month, three-month, and six-month expirations simultaneously.

The premium has historically been structural rather than sentimental. Equity derivatives desks participate in the *dispersion trade*: selling index-level volatility while buying single-stock vol on the largest, most liquid names — a mechanical bid that elevates Mag 7 implied vol relative to smaller constituents. Nvidia (NVDA), which alone represents roughly 9% of the Nasdaq 100, generates quasi-macro hedging demand before every earnings print, bidding up both put and call premium. Portfolio concentration rules add another layer: with the Mag 7 accounting for roughly 35–45% of the S&P 500 by market cap, institutional risk managers maintain standing options overlays on these names that managers of smaller positions simply do not replicate.

The disruption of that premium reflects a shift in where the options market believes the next meaningful move will originate. The Nasdaq 100 staged roughly a 28% rally from its late-March 2026 lows through mid-May, but the Mag 7 basket moved roughly sideways as a group after its Q1 2026 earnings. The velocity came from semiconductor and AI-infrastructure names outside the core basket: implied volatility on chip-sector constituents surged to the 40–45 vol range in early May as call buyers reached for upside in names viewed as closer to the next AI leg. Goldman Sachs (GS) derivatives analyst Cullen Morgan had foreshadowed this in October 2025, noting that roughly 20% of S&P 100 stocks had inverted *call skew* — out-of-the-money calls trading at higher implied vol than at-the-money — against a historical base rate of just 3%, and warning that such readings historically “have coincided with short-term consolidation or reversals as optimism peaks.”

At -9.61 versus a long-run mean of +4.15, the spread implies roughly 14 vol points of potential mean reversion. Derivatives strategists typically read extreme *vol spread* readings as simultaneous statements about relative value and market psychology. Mag 7 upside is relatively cheap on a multi-month horizon if the AI narrative re-centers on the core names; the premium now embedded in smaller-cap NDX upside vol may represent the late-cycle breadth expansion — new speculative names pulling call demand away from the original trade — that has historically preceded corrections. The practical mean-reversion position is to own Mag 7 three-to-six month 25-delta calls against short upside in non-Mag 7 NDX names; the key risk is that the inversion persists, signaling the market has durably re-rated which companies are expected to lead the next AI cycle.

concepts.definition: The market's forward-looking estimate of how much a security will move, extracted from the price of options contracts. It is the volatility figure that, plugged into a pricing model, produces the observed option price. Higher implied vol means options are more expensive; lower means they are cheaper. Expressed as an annualized percentage.

An out-of-the-money call option whose delta — its sensitivity to the underlying stock price — is approximately 0.25, implying roughly a 25% probability of finishing in-the-money. The 25-delta call is the global options market's standard reference point for measuring how much premium buyers will pay for upside exposure beyond the current stock price.

A unit of implied volatility equal to one percentage point of annualized vol. A spread of -9.61 vol points means the Mag 7 basket's upside implied vol is 9.61 percentage points below the comparison group's — a large and historically extreme difference.

A derivatives strategy in which a desk sells index-level volatility (e.g., VIX futures) while buying single-stock implied volatility on the index's largest constituents, betting the index will be calmer than its parts. This creates a structural mechanical bid that tends to inflate implied vol on mega-cap names like the Mag 7 relative to smaller constituents.

In equity options markets, normal skew means put options at equivalent strikes trade at higher implied vol than calls, because investors pay a premium to hedge downside. Inverted or positive call skew occurs when out-of-the-money calls trade at higher implied vol than equivalent puts, signaling aggressive directional call-buying. Goldman Sachs found roughly 20% of S&P 100 stocks in this state in October 2025, versus a historical norm of 3%.

The difference in implied volatility between two securities, baskets, or market segments. Traders can position for a vol spread to converge toward its historical average — buying the relatively cheaper implied vol and selling the relatively more expensive. Goldman Sachs's chart measures the Mag 7 vs. NDX single-stock upside vol spread going back to 2014.

A grouping of seven mega-cap technology companies — Apple, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta Platforms, Nvidia, and Tesla — that together account for roughly 35–45% of the S&P 500 by market capitalization and an even larger share of the Nasdaq 100. The term entered wide use from 2023 onward as these names drove the majority of U.S. equity index returns.
